body.en:
• Outlier Sensitivity (Mean vs. Median): The mean is heavily pulled by extreme outliers, whereas the median is resistant. If an unusually high score is added to a dataset, the mean increases significantly, but the median often changes little or not at all.
  • Expected Value (Net vs. Gross): On ACT raffle/carnival game problems, expected value is \( E(X) = \sum [x \cdot P(x)] \). Watch out whether the question asks for net winnings (subtracting the ticket cost) or gross payout!
  • Mutually Exclusive vs. Independent: For mutually exclusive events, \( P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) \). For non-mutually exclusive events, you must subtract the overlap: \( P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) \). For independent events, \( P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \times P(B) \).
  • Combinations vs. Permutations: Order matters \( \implies \) Permutation \( _nP_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!} \) (e.g. officer positions: President, VP, Secretary). Order does NOT matter \( \implies \) Combination \( _nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!} \) (e.g. committee, team, selecting toppings).

question.en: A data set is: 4, 7, 7, 9, 12, 15. Find the mean, median, and range.

A carnival game costs $5 to play. There is a \(\frac{1}{10}\) probability of winning $30, a \(\frac{2}{10}\) probability of winning $10, and a \(\frac{7}{10}\) probability of winning nothing. What is the expected net profit or loss per play?

solution.en: The expected gross payout is \(E(\text{gross}) = 30\left(\frac{1}{10}\right) + 10\left(\frac{2}{10}\right) + 0\left(\frac{7}{10}\right) = 3 + 2 + 0 = \$5\). Since the ticket costs $5, the expected net profit is \(5 - 5 = \$0\) (a fair game).

question.en: A committee of 3 students is to be chosen from a group of 8 candidates. How many different committees can be formed?

solution.en: Because the order of committee members does not matter, this is a combination: \(_8C_3 = \dfrac{8!}{3!(8-3)!} = \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 56\) different committees.
